title: Cofibrant inputs and fibrant right adjoints of a dg Quillen bifunctor
statement:
Let $\mathcal M,\mathcal N,\mathcal P$ be combinatorial differential graded model categories: complete and cocomplete locally presentable categories enriched, tensored and cotensored over unbounded complexes of abelian groups [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with model structures satisfying the model and enrichment axioms of [lem-coef-dg-model-mapping-comparison]. No stability is assumed. Let $B:\mathcal M\times\mathcal N\to\mathcal P$ be an enriched two-variable left adjoint. Write $A(Q,-)$ and $A'(P,-)$ for its enriched right adjoints, specified by natural isomorphisms of complexes
$$\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal P}(B(P,Q),I)\cong\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal M}(P,A(Q,I))\cong\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal N}(Q,A'(P,I)).$$
Assume that for cofibrations $i:P\to P'$ and $j:Q\to Q'$ the pushout-product map
$$B(P',Q)\amalg_{B(P,Q)}B(P,Q')\longrightarrow B(P',Q')$$
is a cofibration, trivial when either $i$ or $j$ is trivial, where trivial means also a weak equivalence. Then $B(P,Q)$ is cofibrant for cofibrant $P,Q$; for each cofibrant $Q$, $B(-,Q)$ preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations, and for each cofibrant $P$, $B(P,-)$ does likewise. For cofibrant $Q$ and fibrant $I$, $A(Q,I)$ is fibrant; for cofibrant $P$ and fibrant $I$, $A'(P,I)$ is fibrant.

proof.text: Let $0_{\mathcal M}$ and $0_{\mathcal N}$ be the initial objects. Each partial functor of the two-variable left adjoint $B$ is a left adjoint, so it preserves initial objects; hence $B(0_{\mathcal M},Q)$, $B(P,0_{\mathcal N})$, and $B(0_{\mathcal M},0_{\mathcal N})$ are initial in $\mathcal P$. By [lem-coef-dg-model-mapping-comparison], cofibrancy means that the initial map is a cofibration. For cofibrant $P,Q$, the maps $i:0_{\mathcal M}\to P$ and $j:0_{\mathcal N}\to Q$ are cofibrations, and their pushout product is canonically the initial map $0_{\mathcal P}\to B(P,Q)$. The assumed pushout-product axiom therefore makes $B(P,Q)$ cofibrant.

proof.text: Fix a cofibrant $Q$ and let $i:P\to P'$ be a cofibration in $\mathcal M$. Use $j:0_{\mathcal N}\to Q$. The initiality of $B(P,0_{\mathcal N})$ and $B(P',0_{\mathcal N})$ identifies the pushout product $i\mathbin{\square_B}j$ with $B(i,Q):B(P,Q)\to B(P',Q)$. Thus the hypothesis makes $B(-,Q)$ preserve cofibrations, and when $i$ is also a weak equivalence it makes $B(i,Q)$ a trivial cofibration. The same argument with the two variables interchanged proves that $B(P,-)$ preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations for every cofibrant $P$.

proof.text: Fix cofibrant $Q$ and a fibration $p:I\to J$ in $\mathcal P$. Apply [lem-coef-parametrized-adjunction-corner-lifting] to the parametrized adjunction with $H(c,d)=B(d,c)$ and $R(c,e)=A(c,e)$, with the first arrow $0_{\mathcal N}\to Q$ and the second arrow $u$ in $\mathcal M$. The pushout product is then $B(u,Q)$ by Step 2. For every $I$, the object $A(0_{\mathcal N},I)$ is terminal: maps from any $P$ to it correspond under the adjunction to maps from the initial object $B(P,0_{\mathcal N})$ to $I$, a singleton. Consequently the pullback corner is $A(Q,I)\to A(0_{\mathcal N},I)\times_{A(0_{\mathcal N},J)}A(Q,J)$, canonically $A(Q,p)$. If $u$ is a trivial cofibration, Step 2 makes $B(u,Q)$ a trivial cofibration, hence it lifts against every fibration $p$; the cited lifting equivalence gives that $u$ lifts against $A(Q,p)$, so $A(Q,p)$ is a fibration. If $p$ is a trivial fibration, the same argument with arbitrary cofibrations $u$ and the cofibration part of Step 2 shows that $A(Q,p)$ is a trivial fibration. A right adjoint preserves the terminal object, so for fibrant $I$ the map $A(Q,I)\to A(Q,*)=*_{\mathcal M}$ is a fibration; thus $A(Q,I)$ is fibrant.

proof.text: Interchange $\mathcal M$ and $\mathcal N$ and use the other enriched right adjunction $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal P}(B(P,Q),I)\cong\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal N}(Q,A'(P,I))$. The argument of Step 3, with $H(c,d)=B(c,d)$ and $R(c,e)=A'(c,e)$, shows that $A'(P,-)$ preserves fibrations and trivial fibrations whenever $P$ is cofibrant. Since it preserves the terminal object, a fibrant $I$ gives a fibration $A'(P,I)\to *_{\mathcal N}$, so $A'(P,I)$ is fibrant.
